title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第14部分：扩散与流

chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现

5c3a0598887c.en: Noise. A cloud of random points. <bookmark mark='a'/> Now a network, trained on this computer, nudges each point a little, again and again. <bookmark mark='b'/> In part four we did this with the exact answer written in. This time, the network had to learn it from examples.
5c3a0598887c.zh: 噪声。一团随机的点。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在，一个就在这台电脑上训练出来的网络，把每个点轻轻推一下，一遍又一遍。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第4部分，我们也这样做过，但那时精确的答案是直接写进去的。这一次，网络得从例子里自己学出来。

827e3ca7a84c.en: This part is about how image, video and now even text models make things from noise: what the network learns, how to walk back, why straight paths are faster, how to ask for something specific, <bookmark mark='a'/> and how to do it for words.
827e3ca7a84c.zh: 这一部分讲的是，图像模型、视频模型，如今甚至还有文本模型，是怎样从噪声中造出东西来的：网络学到的是什么，怎样往回走，为什么直的路径更快，怎样要它画出某个特定的东西，<bookmark mark='a'/>以及怎样把这一切用在文字上。

27bf98b14860.en: In part four, we ran Brownian motion backwards to turn noise into the letters A I, but we cheated: we computed the score, the uphill direction of the data's density, from the data itself. A real model has to learn it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's how. Take a data point, add a random amount of noise. <bookmark mark='b'/> Train a network to look at the noisy point and guess the noise that was added. That's all: a regression. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the guess, divided by the noise level, turns out to be exactly the score. Learning to denoise is learning the arrows.
27bf98b14860.zh: 在第4部分，我们让布朗运动倒着跑，把噪声变成了字母A和I，但我们作了弊：分数函数，也就是数据密度的上坡方向，是我们直接从数据本身算出来的。真正的模型得把它学出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>方法是这样的。取一个数据点，加上随机大小的噪声。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练一个网络，让它看着这个带噪声的点，猜出加进去的噪声。就这么简单：一个回归问题。<bookmark mark='c'/>而这个猜测，除以噪声水平，结果恰好就是分数函数。学会去噪，就是学会那些箭头。

64b3af12946c.en: Picture the data's density as a landscape over the plane. <bookmark mark='a'/> Under heavy noise, it's one smooth hill. <bookmark mark='b'/> Take the noise away, step by step, and the hill splits and sharpens into ridges, in the shape of the letters. The score is simply the uphill direction on this landscape, at every noise level. That's what the network has to learn.
64b3af12946c.zh: 把数据的密度想象成平面上的一片地形。<bookmark mark='a'/>噪声很大时，它是一座平滑的山丘。<bookmark mark='b'/>把噪声一步步去掉，这座山就分裂开来，变得越来越陡，成为一道道山脊，形状就是那些字母。分数函数，就是这片地形在每个噪声水平下的上坡方向。网络要学的，就是这个。

f884fbdbe4ec.en: Here are the arrows our trained network draws. <bookmark mark='a'/> At high noise, they all point roughly towards the middle: from far away, the data is one blob. <bookmark mark='b'/> As the noise drops, the arrows bend towards the letters, <bookmark mark='c'/> and at low noise they point to the nearest stroke. One network, told the noise level, knows the right arrows for every level: that's what a sampler needs to walk from noise to data.
f884fbdbe4ec.zh: 这是我们训练好的网络画出的箭头。<bookmark mark='a'/>噪声很大时，它们都大致指向中间：从远处看，数据就是一团。<bookmark mark='b'/>随着噪声减小，箭头弯向那些字母，<bookmark mark='c'/>到噪声很小时，它们指向最近的那一笔。一个网络，只要告诉它噪声水平，就知道每个水平下正确的箭头：采样器要从噪声走到数据，需要的正是这个。

e0e8979b291f.en: How does a denoiser learn this? Here is ours being trained. At each checkpoint, we stop, and use it to draw six hundred points from the same noise. <bookmark mark='a'/> Untrained, it flings them all over the place. <bookmark mark='b'/> Within 50 steps it already has the rough shape: the loss plunges in the first hundred steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> The rest of training is refinement. The loss barely moves, but the strokes keep sharpening: the distance from the data goes from 0.24 to 0.15, not smoothly, but on the whole. Each step only ever asked it to guess the noise in one blurred point; the shape emerges from millions of those guesses.
e0e8979b291f.zh: 去噪器是怎样学会这一点的？这是我们的去噪器在训练中的样子。在每个检查点，我们停下来，用它从同一份噪声里画出600个点。<bookmark mark='a'/>还没训练时，它把这些点甩得到处都是。<bookmark mark='b'/>不到50步，它就已经有了大致的形状：损失在前100步里急剧下降。<bookmark mark='c'/>剩下的训练都是在精修。损失几乎不动，但笔画一直在变清晰：与数据的距离从0.24降到0.15，不是平稳地降，而是总体上在降。每一步只要求它猜出一个模糊的点里的噪声；形状就从数百万次这样的猜测中浮现出来。

9d30d15b9abb.en: Chapter two. Walking back from noise.

22ca1c63cd60.en: Now walk back. DDPM, the 2020 paper that made diffusion work, takes many small steps: at each, it uses the network to guess the clean point, steps partway towards it, and adds a little fresh noise. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its paths wander, like the Brownian motion they reverse. <bookmark mark='b'/> DDIM, a year later, noticed the same network also defines a deterministic path, with no noise added: each point glides to a fixed destination, and in far fewer steps.
22ca1c63cd60.zh: 现在往回走。DDPM，就是2020年那篇让扩散模型真正奏效的论文，它迈很多小步：每一步，都用网络猜出干净的点，朝它走一段，再加上一点新的噪声。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的路径弯弯绕绕，就像它所反转的布朗运动。<bookmark mark='b'/>一年后，DDIM注意到，同一个网络还定义了一条确定性的路径，不加任何噪声：每个点都滑向一个固定的终点，而且需要的步数少得多。

dd8c745e1791.en: How few steps can you take? Measure how far the samples land from the real data, <bookmark mark='w'/> with the sliced Wasserstein distance: drop both clouds onto many random lines, and compare where their points fall. <bookmark mark='a'/> With five DDIM steps, the letters are blurred; by twenty, they're nearly as good as DDPM's two hundred; beyond that, little changes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each step is one run of the network, so fewer steps is faster pictures. Can we do better still? The paths are curved, and curved paths need many small steps.
dd8c745e1791.zh: 最少能走几步？量一量样本落点离真实数据有多远，<bookmark mark='w'/>用的是切片Wasserstein距离：把两团点都投到许多条随机的直线上，比较它们的点落在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>用5步DDIM，字母是模糊的；到20步，就几乎和DDPM的200步一样好；再往后，变化就不大了。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一步都要把网络运行一次，所以步数越少，出图就越快。还能做得更好吗？这些路径是弯的，而弯的路径需要很多小步。

8cdc7bb32f01.en: Flow matching asks for the simplest path there is. Pair a random noise point with a random data point and join them with a straight line. <bookmark mark='a'/> Train a network to output the velocity along that line: just the data point minus the noise point. <bookmark mark='b'/> To sample, start from noise and follow the learned velocity, a few steps at a time. It's the same idea as diffusion, with simpler bookkeeping, and it's what Stable Diffusion 3 and Flux are trained with.
8cdc7bb32f01.zh: 流匹配要的是最简单的路径。把一个随机的噪声点，和一个随机的数据点配成一对，用一条直线连起来。<bookmark mark='a'/>训练一个网络，输出沿着这条直线的速度：就是数据点减去噪声点。<bookmark mark='b'/>采样时，从噪声出发，沿着学到的速度走，一次走几步。它和扩散是同一个想法，只是记账更简单，Stable Diffusion 3和Flux用的正是它。

3c7bb77c7849.en: Here are the learned paths. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each training line was straight, but the paths bend. A noise point was paired with a different random data point every time, so the network learns the average direction, and averages of straight lines curve. <bookmark mark='b'/> Curved paths still need many steps.
3c7bb77c7849.zh: 这是学到的路径。<bookmark mark='a'/>每条训练用的线都是直的，但路径却弯了。一个噪声点每次都和一个不同的随机数据点配对，所以网络学到的是平均方向，而直线的平均是会弯的。<bookmark mark='b'/>弯的路径，仍然需要很多步。

181f26d81bb4.en: The fix is called reflow. Run the trained model to pair each noise point with the sample it actually leads to, and train a second model on those pairs. <bookmark mark='a'/> Now the pairs agree with each other, and the paths straighten: from 0.506 to 0.999. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a straight path, one big step lands where a hundred small ones would. That's distillation: a slow teacher model's results become the targets a fast student learns to hit in one go. Distilled this way, image models now make a picture in one to four steps.
181f26d81bb4.zh: 修正的办法叫作重流。运行训练好的模型，把每个噪声点和它实际通向的样本配成一对，再用这些配对训练第二个模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在这些配对彼此一致了，路径也就拉直了：从0.506到0.999。<bookmark mark='b'/>在一条直的路径上，一大步落下的地方，和100个小步落下的地方一样。这就是蒸馏：一个慢的教师模型得出的结果，成为一个快的学生模型要一次命中的目标。经过这样的蒸馏，图像模型如今只要1到4步就能画出一张图。

7a798cb03820.en: Reflow needs a second model and a second round of training. In 2025, MeanFlow found a more direct route. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is one point's path under our flow model: it bends. Flow matching learns v, the velocity at each moment, so it has to take many small steps. <bookmark mark='b'/> MeanFlow learns u instead: the average velocity between two times s and t, like the average speed over a whole trip rather than the speedometer's reading at each moment. <bookmark mark='c'/> With it, a single jump from s to t lands on the path, however much it bends. <bookmark mark='d'/> But to get u exactly we'd have to add up the velocity all along the path, that integral, which is the slow work we wanted to avoid. The trick: write t minus s times u as z t minus z s, and differentiate in s. Out comes an identity: the average velocity is the velocity now, plus a correction, t minus s times how fast the average shifts as the starting point moves along the path. <bookmark mark='e'/> And that correction costs one Jacobian-vector product: how the network's output changes when its input moves in one direction, which costs about one extra run of the network. <bookmark mark='f'/> So the network is trained to match the right-hand side, held fixed, that is treated as a constant target, with no integral and no teacher model.
7a798cb03820.zh: 重流需要第二个模型，还要第二轮训练。2025年，MeanFlow找到了一条更直接的路。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是在我们的流模型下，一个点的路径：它是弯的。流匹配学的是v，也就是每一刻的速度，所以它不得不迈很多小步。<bookmark mark='b'/>MeanFlow学的则是u：两个时刻s和t之间的平均速度，就像整段旅程的平均速度，而不是速度表在每一刻的读数。<bookmark mark='c'/>有了它，从s到t一跳，就能落在路径上，不管路径弯得多厉害。<bookmark mark='d'/>可是要精确得到u，就得把整条路径上的速度都加起来，也就是那个积分，而这正是我们想避免的慢功夫。诀窍是：把t减s乘以u，写成z t减z s，再对s求导。得出一个恒等式：平均速度，等于此刻的速度，加上一个修正项：t减s，乘以起点沿路径移动时，平均速度变化得有多快。<bookmark mark='e'/>而这个修正项，只需要一次雅可比–向量积：输入朝一个方向移动时，网络的输出怎样变化，代价大约是多运行一次网络。<bookmark mark='f'/>所以，网络被训练成去匹配右边那一项，而右边保持固定，也就是被当作一个常数目标，既不需要积分，也不需要教师模型。

d3d6c3c79103.en: Here are all four after a single step from the same noise. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain flow matching lands everything near the middle: one step along the starting velocity is a blur. Reflow does much better. <bookmark mark='b'/> MeanFlow, one jump, reaches 0.171; two jumps, 0.153. <bookmark mark='c'/> Shortcut models, from 2024, get there another way: they're told the size of the jump, and trained so that one jump of size two d equals two jumps of size d. Here the best single step is the reflowed model's. Few-step samplers like these are why image models can now draw in one to four steps.
d3d6c3c79103.zh: 这是4种方法从同一份噪声出发、只走一步之后的结果。<bookmark mark='a'/>普通的流匹配，把所有点都落在中间附近：沿着起始速度走一步，得到的是一片模糊。重流要好得多。<bookmark mark='b'/>MeanFlow，跳一次，达到0.171；跳两次，0.153。<bookmark mark='c'/>2024年的捷径模型，走的是另一条路：告诉它跳跃的大小，并训练它，让一次大小为2d的跳跃，等于两次大小为d的跳跃。在这里，最好的单步结果属于重流后的模型。正因为有这样的少步采样器，图像模型如今才能用1到4步画出图来。

d53e94a36b82.en: So far the model draws whatever it likes. To ask for something, tell it what you want: a caption, or here, which letter. <bookmark mark='a'/> We trained a flow model on two letters, A and I, telling it which letter each training point came from, except one time in five, when it's told nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Told the letter, the model is called conditional; told nothing, unconditional. So one network learns both: the letter it's asked for, and letters in general.
d53e94a36b82.zh: 到目前为止，模型想画什么就画什么。要让它画某样东西，就告诉它你要什么：一段图片说明，或者在这里，是哪个字母。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们在A和I两个字母上训练了一个流模型，告诉它每个训练点来自哪个字母，只是每5次里有1次，什么也不告诉它。<bookmark mark='b'/>告诉了字母，这个模型就叫条件模型；什么都不告诉，就叫无条件模型。所以一个网络同时学会了两样东西：要求它画的那个字母，以及一般意义上的字母。

748b077386bb.en: Now ask for an A, and mix the two answers. At any point, the unconditional model points one way, the conditional one another. Start from the unconditional direction, and push along the difference, towards the conditional one and past it, by a weight w. <bookmark mark='a'/> With w equal to zero, the request is ignored: 47 percent of samples land on the A. <bookmark mark='b'/> With w equal to one, the plain conditional model: 100 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Push past it, to w equal to four, and you overshoot on purpose: 100 percent, and the samples crowd towards the most A-like part of the A, their spread shrinking from 0.93 to 0.69. Every image model turns this knob: more faithful to the prompt, less varied.
748b077386bb.zh: 现在要一个A，并把两个回答混合起来。在任何一点，无条件模型指向一个方向，条件模型指向另一个方向。从无条件的方向出发，沿着两者之差往前推，推向条件的方向，再越过它，推多远由一个权重w决定。<bookmark mark='a'/>w等于0时，要求被忽略了：47%的样本落在A上。<bookmark mark='b'/>w等于1时，就是普通的条件模型：100%。<bookmark mark='c'/>越过它，推到w等于4，就是故意推过头：100%，而且样本挤向A里最像A的那部分，散布从0.93缩小到0.69。每个图像模型都会拧这个旋钮：更忠实于提示词，但变化更少。

371dc9bc9f90.en: Chapter five. From points to pictures.

883da4d570f1.en: Points in a plane were a warm-up. A picture is also a point: here, letters from many fonts, twenty by twenty pixels. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each picture is a list of 400 numbers, one point in a space of 400 dimensions. <bookmark mark='b'/> The model is exactly the one we trained on the A I points, flow matching from noise, just with more numbers.
883da4d570f1.zh: 平面上的点只是热身。一张图片也是一个点：这里是来自许多字体的字母，20乘20像素。<bookmark mark='a'/>每张图片是一串400个数，也就是400维空间里的一个点。<bookmark mark='b'/>模型和我们在A、I那些点上训练的完全一样，从噪声出发做流匹配，只是数多了一些。

9c75cdbe31ea.en: Here's one picture being born. <bookmark mark='a'/> Static, then a blur, then a shape, then a letter. <bookmark mark='b'/> And a batch of samples: rough, speckled, but mostly recognizable capitals, in a mix of styles, not copies of the training pictures. <bookmark mark='c'/> Real image models do the same thing at a million times the scale, in a compressed space of image patches: that's part fifteen.
9c75cdbe31ea.zh: 这是一张图片诞生的过程。<bookmark mark='a'/>先是雪花噪点，然后是一片模糊，然后是一个形状，然后是一个字母。<bookmark mark='b'/>再来一批样本：粗糙、有斑点，但大多是认得出来的大写字母，风格各异，并不是训练图片的复制品。<bookmark mark='c'/>真正的图像模型做的是同样的事，规模大上100万倍，在一个由图像块构成的压缩空间里进行：这是第15部分的内容。

a6f42f835ceb.en: Text isn't made of continuous numbers, so what's the noise? Blanks. Blank out each character with probability t; at t equal to one, everything is blank. <bookmark mark='a'/> The model sees the rest, on both sides, and guesses every blank. Weighted by one over t, that's a bound on the bits per character: a guaranteed ceiling, so the true figure can only be lower. It's the same quantity as on our scoreboard. LLaDA, in 2025, trained an eight-billion-parameter language model this way.
a6f42f835ceb.zh: 文本不是由连续的数构成的，那噪声是什么？是空白。把每个字符以概率t涂成空白；t等于1时，全部都是空白。<bookmark mark='a'/>模型看着剩下的字符，两边的都看，猜出每一个空白。按t分之1加权，这就给出了每字符比特数的一个上界：一个有保证的上限，所以真实的数值只会更低。它和我们记分牌上的是同一个量。2025年，LLaDA就用这种方法，训练了一个80亿参数的语言模型。

95adc77e5f43.en: Here's our own small text diffuser writing 64 characters. It starts with all blanks. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each round it guesses every blank, keeps only the guesses it's surest of, and blanks the rest again. <bookmark mark='b'/> Words appear in no particular order, wherever the model is confident first, and the rest fills in around them. It's a different way to write: all at once, then refined, rather than left to right.
95adc77e5f43.zh: 这是我们自己的小文本扩散模型，正在写64个字符。它从全是空白开始。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一轮，它猜出每一个空白，只保留它最有把握的那些猜测，把其余的重新涂成空白。<bookmark mark='b'/>词语出现的顺序没有什么规律，模型先对哪里有把握，哪里就先出现，其余的再围绕着它们填上。这是一种不同的写法：先一下子全部写出，再慢慢修改，而不是从左往右写。

185f67b69abc.en: Writing everything at once has a cost: the length is fixed in advance, and nothing can be cached. Block diffusion splits the difference. <bookmark mark='a'/> The text is cut into blocks. Within a block, tokens are unmasked a few at a time, as here; <bookmark mark='b'/> across blocks, it goes left to right, like an ordinary language model, so finished blocks can be cached and the text can run as long as it likes. <bookmark mark='c'/> With blocks of one token, it is an ordinary language model; with a single block, it's this chapter's. Commercial diffusion language models, Google's Gemini Diffusion and Inception's Mercury, report writing over a thousand tokens a second.
185f67b69abc.zh: 一下子写出全部内容是有代价的：长度得事先定好，而且什么都没法缓存。块扩散取了个折中。<bookmark mark='a'/>文本被切成一个个块。在一个块之内，词元一次揭开几个，就像这里这样；<bookmark mark='b'/>在块与块之间，则从左往右走，就像普通的语言模型，所以写完的块可以缓存起来，文本想写多长就写多长。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果每块只有1个词元，它就是普通的语言模型；如果只有1个块，它就是这一章的模型。商用的扩散语言模型，Google的Gemini Diffusion和Inception的Mercury，据报告每秒能写出1000多个词元。

107ee4394201.en: Let's take stock. A diffusion model learns to guess the noise in a noisy example, and that guess is the score. DDPM walks back from noise with a little randomness at every step; DDIM walks a fixed path in far fewer. Flow matching learns straight-line velocities, and reflow straightens the paths until one step will do. Guidance turns a request into a push. The same machinery makes pictures, and, with blanks for noise, text.
107ee4394201.zh: 我们来盘点一下。扩散模型学的是猜出带噪声的例子里的噪声，而这个猜测就是分数函数。DDPM从噪声往回走，每一步都带一点随机性；DDIM走的是一条固定的路径，步数少得多。流匹配学的是沿直线的速度，而重流把路径拉直，直到一步就够。引导把一个要求变成一股推力。同一套机制能画出图片，而用空白当作噪声，还能写出文本。

47746251d536.en: Next time this machinery meets real images and video, in a compressed space and with transformers as the denoisers. Speech generators use it too, in part sixteen; world models imagine the next frame with it, in part eighteen; and part nineteen is about making it fast.
47746251d536.zh: 下一次，这套机制要面对真实的图像和视频，在一个压缩的空间里进行，并用Transformer来做去噪器。语音生成器也用它，那是第16部分；世界模型用它来想象下一帧画面，那是第18部分；而第19部分讲的，是怎样让它变快。

b665073ab106.en: Next time: images and video. A picture is cut into patches, and the patches become tokens, <bookmark mark='a'/> so the transformers of part eleven can look at pictures, and denoise them.
b665073ab106.zh: 下一次：图像和视频。一张图片被切成一个个图像块，这些图像块变成词元，<bookmark mark='a'/>这样，第11部分的Transformer就能看图片，并给它们去噪。

9291418c735f.en: Sander Dieleman's blog posts on diffusion are a wonderful companion. Thanks for watching, and see you in part fifteen.
9291418c735f.zh: Sander Dieleman写的那些关于扩散的博客文章，是绝佳的参考读物。感谢观看，我们第15部分再见。
